reports.method: Native original printed banks reread at 4× or 2× inspection. Measured guide observations define a shape-preserving cubic search corridor; original unblurred grayscale cross-sections sampled every 5 native pixels, tangent-averaged over 5 pixels, are jointly matched to ink centres within +/-10 pixels using squared offset-change penalty 3 and squared absolute-offset penalty 0.08. The tiny Gedong wedge uses direct measured bank centres without automatic snapping, preserving its paired banks. Shape-preserving cubic interpolation of these measured ink centres is sampled at at most 1.5 pixels. No image blur, classification dilation, freehand geographic polygon or ground-coordinate adjustment. Source guides and full sampled vectors retained; endpoints remain on source-bank reaches. The acute Murai head also uses directly measured bank centres, preserving a single non-crossing pointed source head. Final physical-bank guides were checked against constrained native cross-sections normal to the coast: only the nearest local dark shore-stroke centre within 6 px was read, never text/grid walking. The guide direction identifies the source bank before interpolation.

reports.method: Native original banks reread on 2×–8× source-pixel grids. Shape-preserving vector guides define a +/-7px search corridor; original unblurred raster cross-sections are matched jointly to printed ink centres, using 5px along-ink averaging and continuity penalty 4. Matching is disabled where the other measured bank is within12px, blended to full matching at20px; narrow banks stay on their independently read centres. A vector-offset smoothing spline has <=0.5px RMS fitting allowance, without filtering the raster. Final source-native vectors use shape-preserving interpolation at <=1.5px. Acute paired-bank tips use directly measured source centres to avoid bank collapse. No raster blur, geometric bank widening, modern coastline or fitted ground movement. Pulau Buloh is separately source-traced as a closed component; its existing false mainland membership was checked before addition. Outer bank: Native G11 original-pixel measurements of the physical grey/brown shore stroke. Shape-preserving PCHIP by cumulative guide arclength, sampled at <=2 native px. The Murai mouth/north-head interval between the two open arcs is retained from the existing source outline rather than replaced through an uncertain coastal/marsh boundary. The long northern arc begins at source shore [1394,2300]; its earlier trial hook at [1377,2340] was discarded after 12× source inspection placed that hook inside green/contour ink. Northern arc ends exactly at the mainland Sungei Buloh west-mouth shared junction [2325,1628]. Additional southern-western mangrove and Telok/Kope cape shores, Kranji east outer shore, and the Buloh–Kranji mouth shoulder are direct physical-bank observations from 4–8× native source crops; grid/contour ink and detached brown foreshore islets are excluded. Buloh–Kranji shared endpoints [2478,1644] and [2641.47,1799.05] are retained exactly.

reports.method: Native G16 source-pixel guide vertices read on the original 27521 × 16456 chart, following the physical shore stroke or continuous outer mangrove-tree front. Open arcs replace their corresponding short existing source-ring sections before unchanged registration. Interpolate x and y with shape-preserving PCHIP against cumulative guide arclength, at <=4 native pixels per sample; do not ink-snap to soundings, the printed square grid or individual tree-glyph interiors.
reports.limits: Existing G16 PD-UKGov source and age qualification retained. Mangrove glyph fronts generalise the actual bank; native tracing does not improve external registration accuracy. Kranji water follows visible paired fronts only, closing each head where it narrows into a single printed drainage stroke. No continuation is inferred along the inland single strokes. No G11 or modern coast transplanted. Berih mouth addition follows the paired native mangrove fronts and the clearly blank water corridor around the S. Berih caption. The northern head ends at the transition to the single printed drainage stroke near [7690,5308]; no further eastern line is widened. The southern head ends before stippled ground resumes near [7551,5698]. No printed caption, sounding or isolated mangrove-glyph interior defines the bank. G15/G16 splice policy is unchanged.
